ai.description: The Barmoach frog reaches 4–5 cm. It is olive-brown with dark dorsal spots and a cream-colored belly. Distinctive features include a broad, flattened head and extensively webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Allopaa barmoachensis* is best distinguished from similar species by the presence of distinct, small, black-tipped spines on the chest and forelimbs of breeding males.
ai.habitat: The Barmoach frog inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and rocky mountain brooks, typically found between 1,500 and 2,500 meters amidst dense temperate forest vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Barmoach frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, high-altitude streams of the Himalayas.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Allopaa barmoachensis* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in mountain streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Allopaa barmoachensis* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of the western Himalayas, specifically occurring in Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh at elevations above 2,000m.
ai.callDescription: The Barmoach Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard emanating from rocky streams in high-altitude Himalayan habitats.
